Constructs a cross-species chromatin state reference atlas spanning twelve
mammalian genomes by aligning regulatory regions and projecting a shared
chromatin-state model onto each species. Finds that regulatory elements turn
over substantially faster than coding sequence across the phylogeny, and
shows that single-species conservation claims made from one liftover
frequently do not hold once the full multi-species atlas is consulted.
Released as a versioned, publicly maintained resource.
